question: What is the value of 1 electron volt (eV), which is especially used for nuclear science?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ joules**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1 electron volt (eV)** is a unit of energy commonly used in the field of nuclear science and particle physics.
 
• It is defined as the amount of kinetic energy gained or lost by an electron when it is accelerated through an electric potential difference of one volt.
 
• The value of **1 eV** is **1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ joules**.
 
• This unit is particularly useful because the energies involved in nuclear reactions and particle interactions are typically very small, and using electron volts makes these values more manageable.
 
• The electron volt is not only used in nuclear science but also in various other fields such as solid-state physics and quantum mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of the electron volt was introduced to provide a more convenient unit of energy for atomic and subatomic processes.
 
• In terms of practical applications, electron volts are often used to describe the energy of electrons in electron microscopes, the energy levels of electrons in atoms, and the energy of photons in different regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.
 
• The **joule** (J) is the SI unit of energy, and it is a much larger unit compared to the electron volt.
 
• To convert electron volts to joules, you can use the conversion factor: **1 eV = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ joules**.
 
• Conversely, to convert joules to electron volts, you can use the conversion factor: **1 joule = 6.242 × 10¹⁸ eV**.
